- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven reversal.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1st–3rd day of forecast) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; apply +1–2% bias to first 3 days.
- When sentiment swings from positive to negative, model lags in adjusting; delay forecast correction by 1–2 periods unless sentiment is extreme.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 period horizon; if forecast is >+5% above recent mean, reduce by 1–2% per period until convergence.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) and price is rising, model underestimates; apply +1–2% bias to forecast for next 2–3 periods.
